Hi, thank you for your report!

> The protocol doesn't specify that this must be immediate, however, and I've been writing a Wayland compositor that delays initial configures in certain circumstances.

Are you sure? I always interpreted [the following](https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-shell#xdg_surface) as meaning so:

> After creating a role-specific object and setting it up (e.g. by sending the title, app ID, size constraints, parent, etc), the client must perform an initial commit without any buffer attached. The compositor will reply with initial wl_surface state such as wl_surface.preferred_buffer_scale followed by an xdg_surface.configure event. The client must acknowledge it and is then allowed to attach a buffer to map the surface.

Namely in regards to the "will reply" wording.

If that isn't the case, I guess a quick fix would be to loop (indefinitely?) the roundtrip call until it's configured. I guess that the "will" there means a guarantee. Do you know if other toolkits do a similar thing or are we simply too eager to get an immediate response from the compositor?

> Namely in regards to the "will reply" wording.

I interpreted "will reply" to mean "at some point in the near future" i.e. possibly not in time for a roundtrip.

> Do you know if other toolkits do a similar thing or are we simply too eager to get an immediate response from the compositor?

From what I've gleaned from gtk, instead of spin-looping they wait for the initial configure and map the surface in their configure handler [here](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gtk/-/blob/main/gdk/wayland/gdksurface-wayland.c?ref_type=heads#L984-990). Qt also tracks whether the initial configure is received [here](https://github.com/qt/qtbase/blob/270d54ed387ad53fdaab77d0ad3b274b4dd94199/src/plugins/platforms/wayland/plugins/shellintegration/xdg-shell/qwaylandxdgshell.cpp#L428) and I presume does something similar (haven't dug too far into qt though). Every application I open handles this case correctly except for Godot.

> I interpreted "will reply" to mean "at some point in the near future" i.e. possibly not in time for a roundtrip.

That's fair. I guess the looser interpretation is the safest one.

> From what I've gleaned from gtk, instead of spin-looping they wait for the initial configure and map the surface in their configure handler [here](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gtk/-/blob/main/gdk/wayland/gdksurface-wayland.c?ref_type=heads#L984-990). Qt also tracks whether the initial configure is received [here](https://github.com/qt/qtbase/blob/270d54ed387ad53fdaab77d0ad3b274b4dd94199/src/plugins/platforms/wayland/plugins/shellintegration/xdg-shell/qwaylandxdgshell.cpp#L428) and I presume does something similar (haven't dug too far into qt though). Every application I open handles this case correctly except for Godot.

Thank you for investigating! I'm not sure if an asynchronous solution is possible with our API but I'll try to make it the goal as that seems like the ideal solution. In the meantime I'll add a spinloop with a timeout, hopefully that'll be good enough as a workaround.

I was having a problem with the 4.6.stable editor crashing when opening a specific project.

The "Prefer Wayland" option was checked in the editor settings.
After the crash, I tried using Godot 4.5.stable, but the problem persisted.
All other projects worked normally.
If I uncheck the "Prefer Wayland" option, the project opens normally (except for the known bug with accented keys).

My problem was solved with an unusual solution:
 1. Disable the secondary monitor in the operating system settings.
 2. Open the project in Godot.
 3. Enable the secondary monitor again.

OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS
